claim: Thbs4 is primarily expressed in the SVZ, RMS, and OB in the adult mouse brain.
source: Thbs4 was mainly expressed in the SVZ, RMS, and OB but also in the cerebellum and ventral tegmental area (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Thbs4-positive astrocytes represent 21.4% of the total SVZ cells.
source: After quantification by direct count of Thbs4-positive cells, Thbs4-positive astrocytes represented 21.4% of the total SVZ cells (Figure 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from direct cell counting shown in Figure 1C.

claim: More than 60% of Thbs4-positive cells in the SVZ display a radial glia-like type-B morphology.
source: with more than 60% of them displaying a radial glia-like type-B morphology (Bond et al., 2015; Doetsch et al., 1999; Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological classification data shown in Figure 1D and referenced to prior literature.

claim: Thbs4 expression in B-cells has been reported by immunohistochemistry in previous studies.
source: This is in accordance with other studies reporting Thbs4 expression in B-cells, either by immunohistochemistry (Beckervordersandforth et al., 2010; Benner et al., 2013) or single-cell RNA sequencing (Basak et al., 2018; Cebrian-Silla et al., 2021; Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies using immunohistochemistry and RNA sequencing.

claim: Almost 20% of total cells in the dorsal SVZ expressed GFP 24 hours after postnatal electroporation with pThbs4-eGFP.
source: Twenty-four hours after electroporation, almost 20% of total cells in the dorsal SVZ expressed GFP (Figure 1F)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from electroporation experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Thbs4-positive cells show greater expression in the rostral SVZ compared to other regions.
source: with a greater expression in the rostral SVZ (Figure 1G)
evidence: The claim is supported by regional quantification data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Thbs4 is expressed in NSCs at early postnatal stages, generating astrocytes during development.
source: This also suggests that Thbs4 is expressed in NSCs at early postnatal stages, generating astrocytes during development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the electroporation data showing Thbs4 expression in postnatal NSCs.

claim: Sixty minutes of MCAO caused neuronal damage in the cortex and striatum.
source: Sixty minutes of MCAO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) caused neuronal damage in the cortex and striatum, as observed by cresyl violet staining and NeuN immunofluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The survival rate at 28 days post-lesion was around 50%.
source: The survival rate at 28 days post-lesion was around 50% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Motor deficits improved over time after MCAO.
source: Motor deficits improved over time, while body weight dropped sharply the first 3 days after MCAO and was partially restored at 30 dpi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral assessment data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Body weight dropped sharply the first 3 days after MCAO and was partially restored at 30 dpi.
source: Motor deficits improved over time, while body weight dropped sharply the first 3 days after MCAO and was partially restored at 30 dpi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight monitoring data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The number of actively proliferating NSCs decreases at 7 and 15 dpi in the SVZ, as shown by reduced Nestin levels.
source: The number of actively proliferating neural stem cells (NSCs) and neuroblasts decreases at 7 and 15 dpi in the SVZ, as shown by reduced Nestin (B) and DCX (C) levels, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The number of neuroblasts decreases at 7 and 15 dpi in the SVZ, as shown by reduced DCX levels.
source: The number of actively proliferating neural stem cells (NSCs) and neuroblasts decreases at 7 and 15 dpi in the SVZ, as shown by reduced Nestin (B) and DCX (C) levels, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Thbs4 protein levels increase twofold in the ischemic SVZ at 15 dpi.
source: The increase of Thbs4 astrocytes was also confirmed by western blot analysis using SVZ homogenates (Figure 2E and F), evidencing a twofold increased expression of Thbs4 in the ischemic SVZ.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot quantification data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Nestin protein levels decrease in the SVZ at 15 dpi.
source: Similarly to immunofluorescence, western blot also showed decreased Nestin protein levels at 15 dpi (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot quantification data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The classical pro-neuroblast program of the SVZ is interrupted in favor of the generation of astrocytes after ischemia.
source: These results demonstrate that Thbs4 expression in the SVZ increases after ischemia, coinciding with a decrease in neuroblast markers, suggesting that the classical pro-neuroblast program of the SVZ is interrupted in favor of the generation of astrocytes after ischemia.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data showing increased Thbs4 and decreased neuroblast markers.

claim: BrdU-positive cells increased in the SVZ 24 hours after MCAO.
source: We observed an increase in the number of total SVZ BrdU-positive cells 24 hours after MCAO (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: Ki67-positive cells increased more than tenfold in the SVZ 24 hours after MCAO.
source: Ki67 immunofluorescence of SVZ wholemount preparations also revealed a more than tenfold increase of proliferative cells 24 hours after MCAO (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: Cleaved Caspase3-positive cells significantly increased in the SVZ 24 hours post-lesion.
source: In addition, we observed a significant increase in cleaved Caspase3-positive cells 24 hours post-lesion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cleaved Caspase3 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: There is a fast and specific proliferative response in the ischemia-induced SVZ.
source: These results suggest a fast and specific proliferative response in the ischemia-induced SVZ.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined proliferation and apoptosis data.

claim: There is a twofold increase in the total amount of proliferative cells (BrdU-positive) in the SVZ after MCAO with respect to the sham group.
source: We found a twofold increase in the total amount of proliferative cells (BrdU-positive) after MCAO with respect to the sham group (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU quantification data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No significant change was observed in the number of IdU-positive cells in the SVZ after MCAO.
source: whereas we did not observe a significant change in the number of IdU-positive cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by IdU quantification data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The number of slow proliferative NSC (Thbs4/GFAP/BrdU) increased linearly after MCAO.
source: The number of slow proliferative NSC (Thbs4/GFAP/BrdU) increased linearly after MCAO (Figure 3D and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by triple-labeling quantification data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The number of slow proliferative NSC increased especially in the dorsal region of the SVZ after MCAO.
source: The number of slow proliferative NSC (Thbs4/GFAP/BrdU) increased linearly after MCAO (Figure 3D and E), especially in the dorsal region of the SVZ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by regional quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The number of activated NSC (Thbs4/GFAP/IdU) did not change significantly in the whole SVZ after MCAO.
source: whereas the number of activated NSC (Thbs4/GFAP/IdU) did not change significantly, either in the whole SVZ (Figure 3F) or in any subregion analyzed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by triple-labeling quantification data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: After ischemia, Thbs4-positive astrocytes derive from the slow proliferative type B cells.
source: These results suggest that, after ischemia, Thbs4-positive astrocytes derive from the slow proliferative type B cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential proliferation patterns of BrdU and IdU-labeled cells.

claim: There is a significant decrease in tdTOM-positive cells in the SVZ of ischemic animals at 7, 30, and 60 dpi in all SVZ regions analyzed.
source: After quantification of tdTOM-positive NSCs 7, 30, and 60 dpi, we observed a significant decrease in tdTOM-positive cells in ischemic animals in all SVZ regions analyzed (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by tdTOM quantification data shown in Figure 4B, C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Electroporated cells either left the SVZ area or died after MCAO.
source: After quantification of tdTOM-positive NSCs 7, 30, and 60 dpi, we observed a significant decrease in tdTOM-positive cells in ischemic animals in all SVZ regions analyzed (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that they either left the area or died.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the decrease in tdTOM-positive cells in the SVZ.

claim: There is a general increase of tdTOM-positive cells outside the SVZ after MCAO.
source: Conversely, there was a general increase of tdTOM-positive cells outside the SVZ (Figure 4D and E), especially in the intermediate and caudal axis of the whole brain compared to sham animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F)
evidence: The claim is supported by tdTOM quantification data shown in Figure 4D, E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Electroporated cells migrated away from the SVZ after MCAO.
source: Conversely, there was a general increase of tdTOM-positive cells outside the SVZ (Figure 4D and E), especially in the intermediate and caudal axis of the whole brain compared to sham animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F), suggesting that electroporated cells had migrated away from the SVZ.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the increase in tdTOM-positive cells outside the SVZ.

claim: The fraction of Thbs4/tdTOM cells increased at 30 dpi after MCAO in the SVZ.
source: Despite the general decrease of tdTOM-positive cells in the SVZ, the fraction of Thbs4/tdTOM cells increased at 30 dpi after MCAO (Figure 4F and G)
evidence: The claim is supported by double-labeling quantification data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: The fraction of Thbs4/tdTOM cells reached a maximum increase at 60 dpi after MCAO.
source: Despite the general decrease of tdTOM-positive cells in the SVZ, the fraction of Thbs4/tdTOM cells increased at 30 dpi after MCAO (Figure 4F and G), reaching a maximum increase at 60 dpi (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by double-labeling quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The increase in Thbs4/tdTOM cells occurred in particular in rostral and intermediate SVZ.
source: reaching a maximum increase at 60 dpi (Figure 4H), in particular in rostral and intermediate SVZ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by regional quantification data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: More than half of the total tdTOM-positive cells in the infarcted area expressed the Thbs4 marker at 60 dpi.
source: Finally, we analyzed the Thbs4-positive astrocytes recruitment to the ischemic regions. More than half of the total tdTOM-positive cells in the infarcted area expressed the Thbs4 marker at 60 dpi (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by double-labeling quantification data shown in Figure 4I and J.

claim: Ischemia-induced astrogliogenesis in the SVZ occurs in type B cells from the dorsal region.
source: These results suggest that ischemia-induced astrogliogenesis in the SVZ occurs in type B cells from the dorsal region and that these newborn Thbs4-positive astrocytes migrate to the ischemic areas.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the electroporation and migration data.

claim: Newborn Thbs4-positive astrocytes migrate to the ischemic areas.
source: These results suggest that ischemia-induced astrogliogenesis in the SVZ occurs in type B cells from the dorsal region and that these newborn Thbs4-positive astrocytes migrate to the ischemic areas.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the electroporation and migration data.

claim: Nestin is rapidly and locally expressed by reactive astrocytes and participates in glial scar formation.
source: Besides its role in the neurogenic niches, Nestin is also rapidly and locally expressed by reactive astrocytes and participates in glial scar formation (Frisén et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Nestin immunofluorescence can be used to identify the lesion border where the glial scar occurs.
source: Thus, we used Nestin immunofluorescence as a reliable tool to identify the lesion border where the glial scar occurs (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 5A.

claim: TTC staining underestimates ischemic regions compared with Nestin immunofluorescence.
source: Nestin staining of the scar was also compared with more classical methodologies like TTC staining (Figure 5B), where viable tissue is stained red and dead tissue is left unstained.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A rapid formation of the glial scar occurs as early as 7 dpi.
source: We observed a rapid formation of the glial scar as early as 7 dpi (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course imaging data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: GFAP expression increased rapidly after 7 days within the glial scar ROI.
source: GFAP expression increased rapidly after 7 days within the glial scar ROI, whereas Thbs4 was upregulated at 15 dpi (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Thbs4 was upregulated at 15 dpi within the glial scar ROI.
source: GFAP expression increased rapidly after 7 days within the glial scar ROI, whereas Thbs4 was upregulated at 15 dpi (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The glial scar harbors two different astrocytic subpopulations: GFAP-only or GFAP/Thbs4.
source: This delay suggested that the glial scar harbors two different astrocytic subpopulations: GFAP-only or GFAP/Thbs4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential temporal dynamics of GFAP and Thbs4 expression.

claim: GFAP is found in both the scar and core areas at 30 dpi.
source: GFAP was found in both the scar and core areas, whereas Thbs4 fluorescence was found mostly at the borders of the glial scar (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity profile analysis shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: Thbs4 fluorescence is found mostly at the borders of the glial scar at 30 dpi.
source: GFAP was found in both the scar and core areas, whereas Thbs4 fluorescence was found mostly at the borders of the glial scar (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence intensity profile analysis shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: There is a linear increase of Thbs4-positive astrocytes from 7 to 60 dpi in the cortex and striatum.
source: We observed a linear increase of Thbs4-positive astrocytes from 7 to 60 dpi, both in the Ctx and Str (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Migration of Thbs4-positive astrocytes occurs mainly through the corpus callosum.
source: Migration occurred mainly through the corpus callosum; among the total GFAP-positive astrocytes, 36.5% were also positive for Thbs4
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data showing the proportion of Thbs4/GFAP double-positive cells in the corpus callosum.

claim: More than one-third of the astrocytes in the glial scar originated from the SVZ.
source: Migration occurred mainly through the corpus callosum; among the total GFAP-positive astrocytes, 36.5% were also positive for Thbs4, suggesting that more than one-third of the astrocytes in the glial scar originated from the SVZ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the proportion of Thbs4/GFAP double-positive cells.

claim: The number of DCX-positive cells dramatically decreased 15 dpi in all OB layers.
source: Likewise, the number of DCX-positive cells dramatically decreased 15 dpi in all OB layers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–F)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–F.

claim: There is a significant decrease of BrdU-positive cells in the RMS after MCAO.
source: together with a significant decrease of BrdU-positive cells and DCX/BrdU-positive neuroblasts in the RMS (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: There is a significant decrease of DCX/BrdU-positive neuroblasts in the RMS after MCAO.
source: together with a significant decrease of BrdU-positive cells and DCX/BrdU-positive neuroblasts in the RMS (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: Ischemia induces a change in the neuroblasts' ectopic migratory pathway, depriving the OB layers of SVZ newborn neurons.
source: This suggests that ischemia induced a change in the neuroblasts' ectopic migratory pathway, depriving the OB layers of SVZ newborn neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the decreased neuroblast numbers in the OB and RMS.

claim: Following ischemic damage, local astrocytes (GFAP+/Thbs4-) react by adopting a fibrotic morphology, producing high-molecular weight HA (HMW-HA) to form the glial scar and isolate the damaged area.
source: Following ischemic damage, local astrocytes (GFAP+/Thbs4-) react by adopting a fibrotic morphology, producing high-molecular weight HA (HMW-HA) to form the glial scar and isolate the damaged area (Preston and Sherman, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Skeleton analysis identified progressively longer HA cable-like structures at the glial scar as the infarct evolved.
source: Skeleton analysis, which quantifies the length of HA chains and correlates with its molecular weight, identified progressively longer HA cable-like structures at the glial scar as the infarct evolved (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeleton analysis data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Fractal dimension analysis confirmed HA accumulation and increased matrix complexity in infarcted areas, but not in corpus callosum.
source: Fractal dimension analysis, which reflects the interconnectivity of the ECM (Soria et al., 2020), further confirmed HA accumulation and increased matrix complexity in infarcted areas, but not in corpus callosum (Figure 6C)
evidence: The claim is supported by fractal dimension analysis data shown in Figure 6C and referenced to previous methodology.

claim: ECM accumulation is different in white and gray matter.
source: Fractal dimension analysis, which reflects the interconnectivity of the ECM (Soria et al., 2020), further confirmed HA accumulation and increased matrix complexity in infarcted areas, but not in corpus callosum (Figure 6C), suggesting that ECM accumulation is different in white and gray matter.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential ECM accumulation patterns in different brain regions.

claim: There is a significant increase in HABP area at Thbs4-positive astrocyte-cell membranes after MCAO.
source: Image analysis showed a significant increase in HABP area at Thbs4-positive astrocyte-cell membranes after MCAO (Figure 6G)
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane-associated HA quantification data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Thbs4-positive astrocytes play a role in HA production within the glial scar.
source: Image analysis showed a significant increase in HABP area at Thbs4-positive astrocyte-cell membranes after MCAO (Figure 6G), suggesting a role of Thbs4-positive astrocytes in HA production within the glial scar.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased membrane-associated HA on Thbs4-positive cells.

claim: HMW-HA cleavage occurs extracellularly.
source: While HMW-HA cleavage occurs extracellularly, HA fragments can be internalized for degradation by lysosomal hyaluronidases (Preston and Sherman, 2011; Zimmermann and Dours-Zimmermann, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: HA fragments can be internalized for degradation by lysosomal hyaluronidases.
source: While HMW-HA cleavage occurs extracellularly, HA fragments can be internalized for degradation by lysosomal hyaluronidases (Preston and Sherman, 2011; Zimmermann and Dours-Zimmermann, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Thirty days after MCAO, Thbs4-positive astrocytes showed more intracellular HABP than local astrocytes in the infarcted cortex.
source: Thirty days after MCAO, Thbs4-positive astrocytes showed more intracellular HABP than local astrocytes in the infarcted cortex (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by intracellular HABP quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The number of HA spots internalized was higher in local astrocytes compared with Thbs4 astrocytes.
source: However, the number of HA spots internalized was higher in local astrocytes compared with Thbs4 astrocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by HA spot quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Thbs4-positive cells internalize HA in fewer vesicles compared to local astrocytes.
source: However, the number of HA spots internalized was higher in local astrocytes compared with Thbs4 astrocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that Thbs4-positive cells internalize HA in fewer vesicles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential HA spot numbers between cell types.

claim: CD44 is a transmembrane glycoprotein receptor that mediates HA internalization and degradation, and therefore ECM remodeling.
source: CD44 is a transmembrane glycoprotein receptor that mediates HA internalization and degradation, and therefore ECM remodeling (Dzwonek and Wilczynski, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Around 50% of the total Thbs4-positive astrocytes contained internalized CD44 receptor in the striatum 30 dpi.
source: We detected that around 50% of the total Thbs4-positive astrocytes contained internalized CD44 receptor in the striatum 30 dpi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by CD44 quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: 60% of Thbs4-positive astrocytes contained internalized CD44 receptor in the infarcted corpus callosum.
source: We detected that around 50% of the total Thbs4-positive astrocytes contained internalized CD44 receptor in the striatum 30 dpi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), with higher numbers (60%) for the infarcted corpus callosum.
evidence: The claim is supported by CD44 quantification data.

claim: Thbs4-positive astrocytes participate in both the formation and degradation of the ECM at the glial scar.
source: These findings suggest that Thbs4-positive astrocytes participate in both the formation and degradation of the ECM at the glial scar.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data showing HA synthesis and internalization by Thbs4-positive cells.

claim: Thbs4-positive cells showed increased intracellular HA after OGD in vitro.
source: Thbs4-positive cells showed increased intracellular HA after OGD, while extracellular HA levels decreased (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro HA quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: Extracellular HA levels decreased in Thbs4-positive cells after OGD in vitro.
source: Thbs4-positive cells showed increased intracellular HA after OGD, while extracellular HA levels decreased (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro HA quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: The HA internalization phenomenon was reversed after adding hyaluronidases in the extracellular space.
source: However, this phenomenon was reversed after adding hyaluronidases in the extracellular space (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F and G)
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro HA quantification data with hyaluronidase treatment shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: Thbs4-positive cells from SVZ homogenates can internalize or synthesize HA depending on external stimuli.
source: However, this phenomenon was reversed after adding hyaluronidases in the extracellular space (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F and G), suggesting that Thbs4-positive cells from SVZ homogenates can internalize or synthesize HA depending on external stimuli.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential HA dynamics under different experimental conditions.

claim: HA internalization was reduced in Iba1-positive cell cultures compared to Thbs4-positive cells.
source: HA internalization was also measured in Iba1-positive cell cultures where we observed a reduced internalization compared to Thbs4-positive cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative HA internalization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Metalloproteinase activity was found to be increased in Thbs4 cultures following OGD.
source: Lastly, metalloproteinase activity was found to be increased in Thbs4 cultures following OGD (Figure 6—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by metalloproteinase activity assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Thbs4-positive cells can internalize HA after ischemic conditions but also synthesize it when ECM is degraded.
source: Altogether, these results suggest Thbs4-positive cells can internalize HA after ischemic conditions but also synthesize it when ECM is degraded.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined in vitro experimental results.

claim: Viral-mediated overproduction of HA is sufficient to activate the generation and migration of the Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the SVZ.
source: Here, we show that viral-mediated overproduction of HA, the primary component of the glial scar, is sufficient to activate the generation and migration of the Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the SVZ.
evidence: The claim is supported by the Has2 overexpression experiments.

claim: HA accumulation was sufficient to recruit the Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the ipsilateral SVZ 45 days after AAV-Has2 inoculation.
source: HA accumulation was sufficient to recruit the Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the ipsilateral SVZ 45 days after AAV-Has2 inoculation (Figure 7G)
evidence: The claim is supported by Has2 overexpression and Thbs4 quantification data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: When MCAO was induced and Has2 was overexpressed in the contralateral hemisphere, Thbs4-positive astrocytes preferentially migrated to the ischemic glial scar.
source: Interestingly, when we induced a lesion by MCAO and performed viral overexpression of Has2 in the contralateral hemisphere, we found that Thbs4-positive astrocytes preferentially migrated to the ischemic glial scar (Figure 7G).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative migration data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Migration of Thbs4-positive astrocytes to the site of ischemic damage occurred despite no differences in HA overexpression between contralateral (Has2 infected) and ipsilateral (infarcted area) hemispheres.
source: This migration of Thbs4-positive astrocytes to the site of ischemic damage occurred despite no differences in HA overexpression between contralateral (Has2 infected) and ipsilateral (infarcted area) hemispheres (Figure 7H).
evidence: The claim is supported by HABP quantification data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: The accumulation of HMW-HA alone is sufficient to activate and recruit Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the SVZ.
source: These results suggest that the accumulation of HMW-HA alone is sufficient to activate and recruit Thbs4-positive astrocytes from the SVZ.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Has2 overexpression experiments.

claim: Brain ischemia generates a more potent biochemical signal that not only activates the SVZ but also recruits newborn astrocytes.
source: However, the preferential migration to the ischemic scar indicates that brain ischemia generates a more potent biochemical signal that not only activates the SVZ but also recruits newborn astrocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the preferential migration to the ischemic scar despite equal HA levels.

claim: The niche microenvironment has a unique ECM composition.
source: It is known that the niche microenvironment has a unique ECM composition (Kjell et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The stiffness of the niche plays a crucial role in the proliferation and differentiation of progenitor cells.
source: and that the stiffness of the niche plays a crucial role in the proliferation and differentiation of progenitor cells (Long and Huttner, 2019; Segel et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: HA area decreased at 7 and 15 dpi in the dorsal SVZ.
source: We did not observe any significant changes in the HA area across the entire SVZ but noted a decrease at 7 and 15 dpi in the dorsal SVZ (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by HABP quantification data shown in Figure 8B–D.

claim: Skeleton analysis showed fragmentation of HA exclusively in the dorsal SVZ at 7 and 15 dpi.
source: Skeleton analysis showed fragmentation of HA exclusively in the dorsal SVZ at 7 and 15 dpi (Figure 8E–G)
evidence: The claim is supported by skeleton analysis data shown in Figure 8E–G.

claim: HA fragmentation in the dorsal SVZ occurs earlier than the migration of newborn astrocytes toward the lesion.
source: Skeleton analysis showed fragmentation of HA exclusively in the dorsal SVZ at 7 and 15 dpi (Figure 8E–G), that is, earlier than the migration of these newborn astrocytes toward the lesion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal relationship between HA fragmentation and astrocyte migration.

claim: Hyaluronan degradation genes (Hyal1, Hyal2, and Hyal3) increased by 15 and 30 dpi in the SVZ.
source: We observed an increased expression of all hyaluronidases (Hyal) at 15 dpi and slightly decreased by 30 dpi, whereas synthases (Has) showed a gradual increase from 15 to 30 dpi (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Hyaluronan synthase genes (Has1 and Has2) were overexpressed later, at 30 dpi in the SVZ.
source: We observed an increased expression of all hyaluronidases (Hyal) at 15 dpi and slightly decreased by 30 dpi, whereas synthases (Has) showed a gradual increase from 15 to 30 dpi (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Thbs4 was upregulated at 15 and 30 dpi in the SVZ.
source: Additionally, we observed an upregulation of Thbs4 and Hif1a both at 15 and 30 dpi (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Hif1a was upregulated at 15 and 30 dpi in the SVZ.
source: Additionally, we observed an upregulation of Thbs4 and Hif1a both at 15 and 30 dpi (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: HA degradation in the SVZ is correlated with the Thbs4 response to ischemia.
source: These results suggest that HA degradation in the SVZ is correlated with the Thbs4 response to ischemia.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal correlation between HA degradation and Thbs4 upregulation.

claim: Adult brain stem cells are multipotent and originate from the embryonic radial glia.
source: Adult brain stem cells are multipotent and originate from the embryonic radial glia, thus sharing key cell markers and features with resident astrocytes.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about adult neural stem cells.

claim: In the adult mouse brain, neuroblasts from SVZ migrate through the rostral migratory stream (RMS) to the olfactory bulb (OB), where neurogenesis takes place.
source: In the adult mouse brain, neuroblasts from SVZ migrate through the rostral migratory stream (RMS) to the olfactory bulb (OB), where neurogenesis takes place (Luskin, 1993).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Neuronal hyperactivity (e.g., during epilepsy), as well as pathological conditions (e.g., stroke) or natural (e.g., aging) processes, can impair the physiological functions of the neurogenic niches.
source: Neuronal hyperactivity (e.g., during epilepsy), as well as pathological conditions (e.g., stroke) or natural (e.g., aging) processes, can impair the physiological functions of the neurogenic niches, altering their neurogenic and gliogenic potential (Chaker et al., 2016; Kralic et al., 2005; Sundholm-Peters et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SVZ cells become activated in vivo following focal ischemia induced by middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO).
source: For example, SVZ cells are known to become activated in vivo following focal ischemia induced by middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) (Ceanga et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The ischemic region and the SVZ establish a biochemical interplay based on a gradient of toxic and protective factors released early after the insult.
source: We have previously demonstrated in oxygen and glucose-deprived (OGD) organotypic brain slices that the ischemic region and the SVZ establish a biochemical interplay based on a gradient of toxic and protective factors released early after the insult (Cavaliere et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Brain stroke models in mice can activate astrogliogenesis at the expense of neurogenesis.
source: Furthermore, others have demonstrated that brain stroke models in mice can activate astrogliogenesis at the expense of neurogenesis (Benner et al., 2013; Laug et al., 2019; Li et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Benner and colleagues identified a SVZ-derived astrocyte population characterized by high levels of the membrane-bound proteoglycan thrombospondin 4 (Thbs4).
source: Benner and colleagues identified a SVZ-derived astrocyte population characterized by high levels of the membrane-bound proteoglycan thrombospondin 4 (Thbs4), a cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion molecule that has been considered neuroprotective against ischemic damage (Benner et al., 2013; Laug et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Thbs4 is a cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion molecule that has been considered neuroprotective against ischemic damage.
source: Benner and colleagues identified a SVZ-derived astrocyte population characterized by high levels of the membrane-bound proteoglycan thrombospondin 4 (Thbs4), a cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion molecule that has been considered neuroprotective against ischemic damage (Benner et al., 2013; Laug et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ablation of Thbs4 in KO mice produced abnormal ischemic scar formation and increased microvascular hemorrhage.
source: Ablation of Thbs4 in KO mice also produced abnormal ischemic scar formation and increased microvascular hemorrhage, suggesting a role of SVZ astrogliogenesis in brain damage and glial scar formation induced by ischemic stroke (Benner et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The perilesional barrier known as the glial scar assembles early after brain ischemia, isolating the damaged area and limiting both the spread of pathogens and potentially toxic damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) into the surrounding area.
source: The perilesional barrier known as the glial scar assembles early after brain ischemia, isolating the damaged area and limiting both the spread of pathogens and potentially toxic damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) into the surrounding area (Anderson et al., 2016; Bush et al., 1999; Faulkner et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The glial scar consists of packed reactive astrocytes and a dense extracellular matrix (ECM) composed mostly of hyaluronic acid (HA).
source: Consisting of packed reactive astrocytes and a dense extracellular matrix (ECM) composed mostly of hyaluronic acid (HA), the glial scar represents a physical barrier for the SVZ-generated newborn neurons that migrate into the ischemic core (Arvidsson et al., 2002; Yamashita et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The glial scar represents a physical barrier for the SVZ-generated newborn neurons that migrate into the ischemic core.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Modulating glial scar formation after brain ischemia may be a strategy to reduce tissue damage and restore brain functionality.
source: Thus, modulating glial scar formation after brain ischemia may be a strategy to reduce tissue damage and restore brain functionality.
evidence: The claim is a logical inference based on the role of the glial scar as a barrier.

claim: In ischemic stroke, the brain ECM goes through a significant reorganization due to injury and must undergo successful remodeling to promote brain repair.
source: In ischemic stroke, the brain ECM goes through a significant reorganization due to injury and must undergo successful remodeling to promote brain repair.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about ECM dynamics after injury.

claim: ECM elements involved in the ischemic cascade induce activation of astrocytes and microglia, which modulate ECM structure by releasing glycoproteins into the extracellular space.
source: ECM elements involved in the ischemic cascade induce activation of astrocytes and microglia, which modulate ECM structure by releasing glycoproteins into the extracellular space (Adams and Gallo, 2018; Fawcett, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The crosstalk between ECM elements and glial cells culminates in the formation of the glial scar, which is created locally by reactive astrocytes and astrocytes-secreted ECM molecules such as HA and chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans.
source: This crosstalk culminates in the formation of the glial scar, which is created locally by reactive astrocytes and astrocytes-secreted ECM molecules such as HA and chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (Bush et al., 1999; Lau et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: High extracellular adenosine levels, a hallmark of ischemic insults, induce astrogliogenesis from the SVZ.
source: We have previously demonstrated that high extracellular adenosine levels, a hallmark of ischemic insults, induce astrogliogenesis from the SVZ (Benito-Muñoz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Ischemic conditions increase the number of newly generated astrocytes in the SVZ and their migration to the ischemic area.
source: Following our previous results, here we characterize the SVZ response to brain ischemia and investigate the role of newly generated astrocytes in the modulation of the glial scar after MCAO. We show that ischemic conditions increase the number of newly generated astrocytes in the SVZ and their migration to the ischemic area.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Newborn astrocytes from the SVZ play a role in modulating the ECM at the glial scar.
source: We also propose the role of these astrocytes in modulating the ECM at the glial scar and suggest this astrocyte population as a possible target for brain repair after brain ischemia.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: This astrocyte population is a possible target for brain repair after brain ischemia.

claim: Newborn astrocytes could be a promising pharmacological target for modulating the glial scar after brain ischemia and facilitating tissue regeneration.

claim: Thbs4-positive astrocytes modulate the dense extracellular matrix at the lesion border by both synthesizing and degrading hyaluronan.
source: We found that these Thbs4-positive astrocytes modulate the dense extracellular matrix at the lesion border by both synthesizing and degrading hyaluronan.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The accumulation of hyaluronan at the lesion site is sufficient to recruit newborn astrocytes.
source: We also show that while the accumulation of hyaluronan at the lesion site is sufficient to recruit newborn astrocytes, its degradation at the SVZ correlates with gliogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by the Has2 overexpression experiments.

claim: Hyaluronan degradation at the SVZ correlates with gliogenesis.
source: We also show that while the accumulation of hyaluronan at the lesion site is sufficient to recruit newborn astrocytes, its degradation at the SVZ correlates with gliogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by the qPCR and imaging data showing HA degradation and Thbs4 upregulation.

claim: Thbs4 deletion has been shown to impair migration of SVZ-derived cells along the RMS.
source: It is likely that SVZ-derived newborn astrocytes require Thbs4 expression to facilitate their migration to the ischemic area, as Thbs4 deletion has been shown to impair migration of SVZ-derived cells along the RMS (Girard et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

source: Unlike local reactive astrocytes, which are hastily generated and present both at the core and periphery of the lesion, the newborn astrocytes from the SVZ arrive later to the injury.

claim: Adenosine stimulates astrogliogenesis through A1 receptors following OGD in vitro and ischemia in vivo.
source: We previously identified adenosine, a by-product of ATP hydrolysis, as a strong candidate, as it stimulates astrogliogenesis through A1 receptors following OGD in vitro and ischemia in vivo (Benito-Muñoz et al., 2016).
